body: First time contributor here, can I try to help?

> This problem does not occur when using GodotPhysics3D.

Looking at the `Memory / Static` monitor in the built-in debugger, I'm seeing largely the same behavior with Godot Physics.

However, Godot Physics allocates much less memory per space, which almost certainly stems from the Jolt physics server allocating 32 MiB as a temporary buffer (as dictated by the [`limits/temporary_memory_buffer_size`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-physics-jolt-physics-3d-limits-temporary-memory-buffer-size) project setting) for every physics space. This should probably be shared among them instead, since they'll never be stepped in parallel anyway, which I believe would be the only circumstance when sharing the temporary buffers would be problematic.

There is no automatic garbage collection of physics spaces in either physics server implementation, so there shouldn't be any discrepancy in terms of deallocation.

> Combined with the lack of a PhysicsServer3D method to deallocate/free a space

You have `PhysicsServer3D.free_rid` for freeing any `RID` that the physics server can create, including spaces.

> Looking at the `Memory / Static` monitor in the built-in debugger, I'm seeing largely the same behavior with Godot Physics.

Interesting. In my testing the islands count (which as I understand it is the amount of phyics spaces?) increases with every scene reload, but immediately drops down to 1 shortly after, which to me seemed like it was being cleaned up automatically. With Jolt, that indication didn't increase at all (maybe not implemented?) so it was harder to make sense of the reading.

Regardless, it seems odd to me that GodotPhysics3D only uses a tiny fraction of RAM for every new space, while Jolt's base amount is 32MB (I know it can be lowered, but still, that's orders of magnitude more).

> This should probably be shared among them instead, since they'll never be stepped in parallel anyway

Is this really true though? In my testing, as memory increased, FPS dropped - and not just "once" upon scene loading, but it remained low afterwards (when no further memory allocations were being performed). And it's not like I'm running out of system memory (64GB total), so it seems more to me like all spaces are still present *and being processed in parallel*. Though I'm unsure how that could be, given that I'm calling `queue_free()` on the old scene during the transition...

> You have `PhysicsServer3D.free_rid` for freeing any `RID` that the physics server can create, including spaces.

Huh, no idea how I missed that. Thank you! With manual deallocation of the spaces, my system memory now remains constant (deallocation occurs before the new scene creates a new space). 🥳 

On an unrelated note... I think my strategy of using a new physics space when I load a scene has incured a pleasant side effect: the physics calculations now appear to be fully deterministic. I have a tower of boxes that neatly collapses in the same way everytime the scene is loaded (not just on initial load during game boot). I wonder if this is just a lucky coincidence, or if not, if this could be leveraged directly by the engine? 👀 

**EDIT:** Here's a video showing my test scenario, where the top-most block now always lands in the same position:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66d2595e-eac8-4531-a5e2-d30c6cb3b638

**EDIT 2:** I guess I got too excited about it; after giving it some more thought there isn't anything here that guarantees determinism. So while *I* may be able to achieve the same result on every run, that could still be a strange (albeit pleasant) quirk on my end. So I don't believe Godot can do much about ensuring determinism on the engine side.

> Regardless, it seems odd to me that GodotPhysics3D only uses a tiny fraction of RAM for every new space, while Jolt's base amount is 32MB (I know it can be lowered, but still, that's orders of magnitude more).

It's what's sometimes referred to as a "scratch buffer", that gets reused every physics step, to avoid needing to allocate memory (which can be costly) for stuff that's only used that frame.

The default size of it is (from what I understand) largely correlated to the number of maximum bodies/pairs/contacts/whatever that you expect to see during simulation, so could probably be lowered considerably if you don't expect to have thousands of bodies/pairs.

But again, this should just be shared among all physics spaces instead, at which point 32 MiB isn't all that bad in the greater context.

> Is this really true though?

Yes, as you can see here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34f005d810e8967ee0d57afb78f8e0a64f473094/modules/jolt_physics/jolt_physics_server_3d.cpp#L1579-L1585

If you enable the [`physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-physics-3d-run-on-separate-thread) project setting then the physics server as a whole will be stepped in parallel with things like `_process`, but the spaces themselves will always be stepped in sequence.
